rv.q: This is not the Judy of A Star is Born, it's the Judy of a star in decline. But in Jinkx Monsoon, another star rises.
Monsoon's performance is a triumph, as is Barstow's magnificent band and Prema Mehta's extraordinary lighting design.

While it also lacks momentum, the script is friskier and funnier than the screenplay, with acidic quips and gratuitous name-dropping and shade-throwing (at theatre queen Agatha Christie no less!) but the musical numbers, orchestrated and arranged by Leo Munby, anchor the emotions in the story.
This show gives its audience what they want: but what they want, apparently, is necrophilia.
End of the Rainbow is simply unmissable.

End of the Rainbow sounds heavy — there is no avoiding the sadness that seeped into every corner of Garland’s life — but it’s also incredibly funny thanks to Monsoon’s delightfully sharp tongue and masterful delivery.
A production that is, in most respects, exceptional.
It’s a cruise-ship performance – strong but without shades or colorations.

The Talk of the Town, one of the most glamorous nightclub venues in London at the time, offered Garland a lucrative contract and the possibility of a comeback before wealthy audiences and celebrity admirers.
It is an electrifying introduction, sharply silhouetted against the darkness of our knowledge, and from that moment onward, the audience is utterly locked onto Monsoon’s extraordinary performance.
Monsoon deals with the trappings of fame, addiction, and cycles of abuse elegantly, and it would be foolish to miss a performance of this calibre.
Jinkx's charismatic and slightly unhinged representation of Judy Garland made her joint winner of Snatch Game in RuPaul's Drag Race All Stars season 7, one of the series she later went on to win.
And flawless is how one would also describe Monsoon’s portrayal of Garland, especially in Act II.

cn.t: Jinkx Monsoon's astonishing vocals and commanding presence electrify this revival, though critics split on whether the performance and Peter Quilter's play veer too indulgent, with some finding it uneven despite Monsoon's triumph.
